O.outcome_detail: common factor structure of spatial orientation

result.effect: common Navigation factor captured 32–57% of variance in each test

cells.quote: The six tests correlated substantially and clustered into one common factor, capturing between 32 and 57% of the variance in each individual test, which we named ‘Navigation’, as it indexed abilities that are generally described in the literature as spatial navigation skills

We found that the heritability of the common navigation factor was 64% (95% CIs = 0.41–0.91); shared environmental and nonshared environmental factors accounted for smaller proportions of variance, 8% (95% CIs 0.00 –0.43) and 28% (95% CIs 0.21 –0.36), respectively.

D.comparison: first-order Navigation, Object Manipulation, and Visualization factors

result.effect: R² = 0.79 for Navigation, 0.69 for Object Manipulation, and 1.00 for Visualization

cells.quote: The higher order factor of spatial ability accounted for a large portion of individual differences in the navigation ( R2 = 0.79), object manipulation (R2 = 0.69) and visualization (R2 = 1.00) factors.

O.outcome_detail: genetic variance in the common spatial factor

result.effect: g accounted for 55% of genetic variance; 45% was independent of g

cells.quote: "The results presented in Fig. 7 (see Supplementary Fig. 5 for the full model) showed that g accounted for 55% of the genetic variance in the second-order common spatial ability factor. In other words, 45% of the genetic variance in spatial ability was independent of g."
